key_insight: Water spontaneously self-organizes into 1D double chains in Rb/K titanates, creating fast proton-conducting pathways along the b-axis.
engineering_relevance: The work suggests a crystal-orientation and hydration-controlled route to high room-temperature proton conductivity for solid electrolytes and related energy devices.
method: SEM to observe hydration-dependent surface and pattern formation
Density Functional Theory to model ordered water arrangements and hydrogen bonding
Infrared spectroscopy to support densely packed water chains at hydrated surfaces
evidence_signal: The abstract reports anisotropic superionic proton conductivity reaching 3 mS/cm at room temperature along the b direction after hydration.
watch_item: Conductivity and self-organization appear highly dependent on hydration level and crystal orientation, which may complicate reproducible device fabrication and long-term stability.
paper_title: One-dimensional self-organization of water molecules in proton conducting Andersson-Wadsley titanates
